title: Sampling-based Algorithms for Optimal Motion Planning
page_numbering: PDF pages, 1-based unless locator explicitly refers to printed page

claims.claim: This paper studies geometric path planning in bounded Euclidean space without differential constraints
RRT* chooses a least-cost feasible parent and then rewires neighbors whose root-to-node cost improves
Original radius r_n=min{γ(log n/n)^(1/d),η}; k-nearest alternatives scale with log n, with different algorithm-specific constants
claims.conditions: Original RRT* asymptotic-optimality proof has known later caveat; not asserted as an independently validated proof

claims.claim: Robust feasibility uses positive clearance; robust optimal solution adds weak clearance and local path-cost continuity
PRM* proof uses covering balls, union bounds, summability/Borel–Cantelli and convergence in bounded variation
Original AppendixG RRT* proof was later challenged for confusing pairwise ordering with a globally ordered chain and ignoring steering-induced sample distribution issues
claims.locator: Solovey et al., arXiv:1909.09688v2 §III-B, §IV Remark2 and appendix

claims.claim: Later alternative proof uses radius exponent 1/(d+1), theorem1 probability bound, while tightness relative to 1/d is left open in that paper
claims.conditions: This is a sufficient-condition update, not a counterexample disproving asymptotic optimality at the original radius; not an exhaustive 2026 theory survey

claims.claim: 2D experiments use 500 runs of 20,000 iterations with same sample sequences for RRT/RRT*
5D uses 100 trials; 10D obstacle experiment uses 25 trials
Original fixed-dimension complexity analysis yields O(log n) expected collision calls per iteration and O(n) tree storage
claims.conditions: Specified near-neighbor/range-search models and fixed environment; does not imply a dimension-independent small wall-time constant or carry unchanged to later larger radius

claims.claim: Learned sampling must retain coverage conditions and collision verification; geometric plans require a separate execution/control layer
claims.locator: Reader synthesis based on §2–3 and §6 scope

scope_notes: All original technical sections and appendices read; this is not formal proof verification.
Supplementary critical paper read selectively for its logical gap, theorem statement, conclusion and counterexample; not counted as a new full-reading baseline.
No claim that finite experiments prove asymptotic convergence.
No source PDF or original diagrams redistributed.
